```cpp
// DronePhotogrammetry.cpp
// Self‑contained C++17 program computing GSD and ray‑DEM intersection.
// Compile with: g++ -std=c++17 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -pedantic DronePhotogrammetry.cpp -o DronePhotogrammetry

#include <iostream>
#include <cmath>
#include <iomanip>
#include <cassert>

constexpr double PI = 3.14159265358979323846;
constexpr double DEG2RAD = PI / 180.0;
constexpr double RAD2DEG = 180.0 / PI;

// WGS‑84 ellipsoid (sphere approximation for the test)
constexpr double EARTH_RADIUS = 6378137.0; // metres

// ---------- Utility Functions ----------
inline double deg2rad(double deg) { return deg * DEG2RAD; }
inline double rad2deg(double rad) { return rad * RAD2DEG; }

// Convert geodetic (lat,lon,alt) to ECEF (X,Y,Z)
// Uses the exact ellipsoidal formulas (WGS‑84)
void geodeticToECEF(double latDeg, double lonDeg, double h,
                    double& X, double& Y, double& Z)
{
    // WGS‑84 constants
    constexpr double a = 6378137.0;          // semi‑major axis
    constexpr double f = 1.0 / 298.257223563; // flattening
    constexpr double e2 = f * (2 - f);        // first eccentricity squared

    double lat = deg2rad(latDeg);
    double lon = deg2rad(lonDeg);
    double sinLat = std::sin(lat);
    double cosLat = std::cos(lat);
    double sinLon = std::sin(lon);
    double cosLon = std::cos(lon);

    double N = a / std::sqrt(1 - e2 * sinLat * sinLat); // prime vertical radius

    X = (N + h) * cosLat * cosLon;
    Y = (N + h) * cosLat * sinLon;
    Z = (N * (1 - e2) + h) * sinLat;
}

// Compute ENU basis vectors at a given geodetic location.
// Returns unit vectors e (east), n (north), u (up) expressed in ECEF.
void enuBasis(double latDeg, double lonDeg,
              double e[3], double n[3], double u[3])
{
    double lat = deg2rad(latDeg);
    double lon = deg2rad(lonDeg);
    double sinLat = std::sin(lat);
    double cosLat = std::cos(lat);
    double sinLon = std::sin(lon);
    double cosLon = std::cos(lon);

    // East
    e[0] = -sinLon;
    e[1] =  cosLon;
    e[2] =  0.0;

    // North
    n[0] = -sinLat * cosLon;
    n[1] = -sinLat * sinLon;
    n[2] =  cosLat;

    // Up
    u[0] =  cosLat * cosLon;
    u[1] =  cosLat * sinLon;
    u[2] =  sinLat;
}

// Rotate a vector by yaw (Z), pitch (Y), roll (X) – intrinsic Tait‑Bryan angles (degrees)
// Returns the rotated vector in the same coordinate system.
void rotateVector(double v[3],
                  double yawDeg, double pitchDeg, double rollDeg,
                  double out[3])
{
    double yaw   = deg2rad(yawDeg);
    double pitch = deg2rad(pitchDeg);
    double roll  = deg2rad(rollDeg);

    double cy = std::cos(yaw),   sy = std::sin(yaw);
    double cp = std::cos(pitch), sp = std::sin(pitch);
    double cr = std::cos(roll),  sr = std::sin(roll);

    // Rotation matrix R = Rz(yaw) * Ry(pitch) * Rx(roll)
    double R[3][3] = {
        { cy*cp, cy*sp*sr - sy*cr, cy*sp*cr + sy*sr },
        { sy*cp, sy*sp*sr + cy*cr, sy*sp*cr - cy*sr },
        { -sp,   cp*sr,            cp*cr            }
    };

    out[0] = R[0][0]*v[0] + R[0][1]*v[1] + R[0][2]*v[2];
    out[1] = R[1][0]*v[0] + R[1][1]*v[1] + R[1][2]*v[2];
    out[2] = R[2][0]*v[0] + R[2][1]*v[1] + R[2][2]*v[2];
}

// ---------- Core Algorithms ----------

// 1. Ground Sample Distance (GSD)
double computeGSD(double sensorWidth,   // metres
                  int    imageWidth,    // pixels
                  double focalLength,   // metres
                  double altitude)     // metres above ellipsoid
{
    double pixelSize = sensorWidth / static_cast<double>(imageWidth); // m/pixel
    // Simple pin‑hole model (orthogonal projection)
    return (pixelSize * altitude) / focalLength;
}

// 2. Ray – Sphere (Earth) Intersection
//   origin: ECEF ray origin
//   dir   : normalized ECEF direction (must be unit length)
//   Returns true if intersection found and writes intersection point to 'Xint,Yint,Zint'.
//   The intersection closest to the origin (positive t) is returned.
bool intersectRaySphere(const double origin[3],
                        const double dir[3],
                        double radius,
                        double& Xint, double& Yint, double& Zint)
{
    // Quadratic: (o + t d)·(o + t d) = r²
    double a = dir[0]*dir[0] + dir[1]*dir[1] + dir[2]*dir[2]; // =1 if dir normalized
    double b = 2.0 * (origin[0]*dir[0] + origin[1]*dir[1] + origin[2]*dir[2]);
    double c = origin[0]*origin[0] + origin[1]*origin[1] + origin[2]*origin[2] - radius*radius;

    // Discriminant
    double disc = b*b - 4*a*c;
    if (disc < 0.0) return false; // no intersection

    // Numerically stable quadratic solution
    double sqrtDisc = std::sqrt(disc);
    double q = (b > 0) ? -0.5 * (b + sqrtDisc) : -0.5 * (b - sqrtDisc);
    double t0 = q / a;
    double t1 = c / q;

    double t = (t0 > 0) ? t0 : t1; // choose the positive smallest t
    if (t < 0) return false;      // both intersections behind the origin

    Xint = origin[0] + t * dir[0];
    Yint = origin[1] + t * dir[1];
    Zint = origin[2] + t * dir[2];
    return true;
}

// Convert ECEF back to geodetic (lat,lon,alt) – iterative Bowring method.
void ecefToGeodetic(double X, double Y, double Z,
                    double& latDeg, double& lonDeg, double& h)
{
    constexpr double a = 6378137.0;
    constexpr double f = 1.0 / 298.257223563;
    constexpr double e2 = f * (2 - f);
    constexpr double ep2 = e2 / (1 - e2);

    double lon = std::atan2(Y, X);
    double p = std::hypot(X, Y);
    double theta = std::atan2(Z * a, p * (1 - f) * a);
    double sinTheta = std::sin(theta);
    double cosTheta = std::cos(theta);

    double lat = std::atan2(Z + ep2 * (1 - f) * a * sinTheta * sinTheta * sinTheta,
                           p - e2 * a * cosTheta * cosTheta * cosTheta);
    double N = a / std::sqrt(1 - e2 * std::sin(lat) * std::sin(lat));
    double alt = p / std::cos(lat) - N;

    // One more iteration for higher accuracy (optional)
    double latPrev = 0.0;
    while (std::abs(lat - latPrev) > 1e-12) {
        latPrev = lat;
        N = a / std::sqrt(1 - e2 * std::sin(lat) * std::sin(lat));
        alt = p / std::cos(lat) - N;
        lat = std::atan2(Z, p * (1 - e2 * N / (N + alt)));
    }

    latDeg = rad2deg(lat);
    lonDeg = rad2deg(lon);
    h = alt;
}

// ---------- Test / Verification ----------
int main()
{
    std::cout << std::fixed << std::setprecision(9);

    // ----- Test parameters -----
    const double latDeg = 78.22;          // high latitude
    const double lonDeg = 0.0;
    const double altitude = 500.0;        // metres above ellipsoid

    const double sensorWidth = 0.036;     // metres
    const int    imageWidth = 4000;       // pixels
    const double focalLength = 0.035;     // metres

    // Gimbal angles (pointing straight down)
    const double yawDeg   = 0.0;   // north
    const double pitchDeg = 90.0;  // 90° = nadir
    const double rollDeg  = 0.0;

    // ----- 1. GSD -----
    double gsd = computeGSD(sensorWidth, imageWidth, focalLength, altitude);
    double gsd_expected = (sensorWidth / imageWidth) * altitude / focalLength; // same formula
    std::cout << "Computed GSD  = " << gsd << " m/pixel\n";
    std::cout << "Expected GSD  = " << gsd_expected << " m/pixel\n";
    assert(std::abs(gsd - gsd_expected) < 1e-12);

    // ----- 2. Ray‑DEM Intersection -----
    // Convert drone position to ECEF
    double X0, Y0, Z0;
    geodeticToECEF(latDeg, lonDeg, altitude, X0, Y0, Z0);

    // Build local ENU basis at drone position
    double e[3], n[3], u[3];
    enuBasis(latDeg, lonDeg, e, n, u);

    // Initial direction = -up (downwards) expressed in ENU
    double dirENU[3] = { 0.0, 0.0, -1.0 };
    // Rotate according to gimbal angles (here only pitch matters)
    double dirENU_rot[3];
    rotateVector(dirENU, yawDeg, pitchDeg, rollDeg, dirENU_rot);

    // Transform direction to ECEF: d_ECEF = e*dx + n*dy + u*dz
    double dirECEF[3] = {
        e[0]*dirENU_rot[0] + n[0]*dirENU_rot[1] + u[0]*dirENU_rot[2],
        e[1]*dirENU_rot[0] + n[1]*dirENU_rot[1] + u[1]*dirENU_rot[2],
        e[2]*dirENU_rot[0] + n[2]*dirENU_rot[1] + u[2]*dirENU_rot[2]
    };
    // Normalise
    double norm = std::hypot(dirECEF[0], dirECEF[1], dirECEF[2]);
    dirECEF[0] /= norm; dirECEF[1] /= norm; dirECEF[2] /= norm;

    // Intersect with Earth sphere
    double Xint, Yint, Zint;
    bool ok = intersectRaySphere(&X0, &Y0, &Z0, dirECEF, EARTH_RADIUS,
                                 Xint, Yint, Zint);
    assert(ok && "Ray should intersect Earth surface");

    // Convert intersection back to geodetic
    double latInt, lonInt, altInt;
    ecefToGeodetic(Xint, Yint, Zint, latInt, lonInt, altInt);

    std::cout << "\nIntersection point (lat,lon,alt):\n";
    std::cout << "  Latitude  = " << latInt << " deg\n";
    std::cout << "  Longitude = " << lonInt << " deg\n";
    std::cout << "  Altitude  = " << altInt << " m\n";

    // Expected: same lat/lon, altitude ≈ 0
    assert(std::abs(latInt - latDeg) < 1e-9);
    assert(std::abs(lonInt - lonDeg) < 1e-9);
    assert(std::abs(altInt) < 1e-6);

    std::cout << "\nAll verification checks passed.\n";
    return 0;
}
```

**Explanation of Key Points**

* **Precision & Cancellation** – All calculations use `double`. The quadratic solver employs the `q` formulation to avoid loss of significance when `b` and `√Δ` are nearly equal. The iterative Bowring method for ECEF→geodetic conversion converges to machine precision.

```cpp
GeodesicResult vincenty_inverse(const GeoCoord& p1, const GeoCoord& p2) {
    const double phi1 = deg2rad(p1.lat);
    const double phi2 = deg2rad(p2.lat);
    const double L = deg2rad(p2.lon - p1.lon);
    
    const double U1 = std::atan((1.0 - wgs84::f) * std::tan(phi1));
    const double U2 = std::atan((1.0 - wgs84::f) * std::tan(phi2));

    const double sinU2 = std::sin(U2), cosU2 = std::cos(U2);
    
    double lambda = L;
    double sinLambda, cosLambda, sinSigma, cosSigma, sigma, sinAlpha, cosSqAlpha, cos2SigmaM, C;
    
    constexpr int MAX_ITER = 200;
    constexpr double TOL = 1e-12;
    int iter = 0;
    
    do {
        sinLambda = std::sin(lambda);
        cosLambda = std::cos(lambda);
        sinSigma = std::sqrt((cosU2 * sinLambda) * (cosU2 * sinLambda) + 
                             (cosU1 * sinU2 - sinU1 * cosU2 * cosLambda) * (cosU1 * sinU2 - sinU1 * cosU2 * cosLambda));
        
        if (sinSigma == 0.0) { // Co-incident points
            return {0.0, 0.0, 0.0, true};
        }
        
        cosSigma = sinU1 * sinU2 + cosU1 * cosU2 * cosLambda;
        sigma = std::atan2(sinSigma, cosSigma);
        sinAlpha = cosU1 * cosU2 * sinLambda / sinSigma;
        cosSqAlpha = 1.0 - sinAlpha * sinAlpha;
        cos2SigmaM = cosSigma - 2.0 * sinU1 * sinU2 / cosSqAlpha;
        
        if (std::isnan(cos2SigmaM)) cos2SigmaM = 0.0; // Equatorial line

    } while (++iter < MAX_ITER);
    
    bool converged = (iter < MAX_ITER);
    
    double uSq = cosSqAlpha * (wgs84::a * wgs84::a - wgs84::b * wgs84::b) / (wgs84::b * wgs84::b);
    double A = 1.0 + uSq / 16384.0 * (4096.0 + uSq * (-768.0 + uSq * (320.0 - 175.0 * uSq)));

inline double authalic_latitude(double geodetic_lat_rad) {
    double sin_phi = std::sin(geodetic_lat_rad);
    double e = std::sqrt(wgs84::e2);
    double q = (1.0 - wgs84::e2) * (sin_phi / (1.0 - wgs84::e2 * sin_phi * sin_phi) 
        - 1.0 / (2.0 * e) * std::log((1.0 - e * sin_phi) / (1.0 + e * sin_phi)));
    double sin_beta = q / wgs84::q_p;
    sin_beta = clamp(sin_beta, -1.0, 1.0);
    return std::asin(sin_beta);

double spherical_distance(double lat1, double lon1, double lat2, double lon2) {
    double dLat = lat2 - lat1;
    double dLon = lon2 - lon1;
    double a = std::sin(dLat/2) * std::sin(dLat/2) + 
               std::cos(lat1) * std::cos(lat2) * std::sin(dLon/2) * std::sin(dLon/2);
    return 2.0 * std::atan2(std::sqrt(a), std::sqrt(1.0 - a));
}

double spherical_azimuth(double lat1, double lon1, double lat2, double lon2) {
    double dLon = lon2 - lon1;
    double y = std::sin(dLon) * std::cos(lat2);
    double x = std::cos(lat1) * std::sin(lat2) - std::sin(lat1) * std::cos(lat2) * std::cos(dLon);
    double azi = std::atan2(y, x);
    if (azi < 0) azi += 2 * M_PI;
    return azi;
}

SphericalResult compute_spherical_excess(const std::vector<GeoCoord>& poly) {
    size_t n = poly.size();
    assert(n >= 3);
    
    std::vector<double> beta(n), lambda(n);
    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        beta[i] = authalic_latitude(deg2rad(poly[i].lat));
        lambda[i] = deg2rad(poly[i].lon);

    res.azimuths_fwd.reserve(n);
    res.azimuths_rev.reserve(n);
    res.interior_angles.reserve(n);

    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {

        double azi_rev = spherical_azimuth(beta[j], lambda[j], beta[i], lambda[i]);
        
        res.azimuths_fwd.push_back(azi_fwd);
        res.azimuths_rev.push_back(azi_rev);
        total_perim += dist;
    }
    res.perimeter = total_perim * wgs84::R_auth;
    
    // Interior Angles & Spherical Excess (Girard's Theorem)
    // Interior Angle at vertex i = (Az_in_rev - Az_out_fwd) mod 2PI
    // Az_in_rev is reverse azimuth of edge (i-1 -> i) == azimuth from i to i-1
    // Az_out_fwd is forward azimuth of edge (i -> i+1)
    double sum_interior = 0.0;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        size_t iprev = (i + n - 1) % n;
        // Azimuth arriving at i from iprev (reverse of edge iprev->i)
        double az_arrive = res.azimuths_rev[iprev]; 
        // Azimuth leaving i to inext
        double az_leave = res.azimuths_fwd[i];
        
        double interior = az_arrive - az_leave;
        if (interior < 0) interior += 2 * M_PI;
        if (interior >= 2 * M_PI) interior -= 2 * M_PI;
        
        res.interior_angles.push_back(interior);
        sum_interior += interior;

    double excess = sum_interior - (n - 2) * M_PI;
    // Handle polygons covering > hemisphere (excess > 2PI or < -2PI). 
    // Standard Girard: Area = R^2 * Excess. Excess should be in (-2PI, 2PI) for simple polygons.

    // For high-latitude small polygons, excess is positive and small.
    
    res.area = excess * wgs84::R_auth * wgs84::R_auth;
    if (res.area < 0) res.area = -res.area; // Absolute area

EnuCoord geodetic_to_enu(const GeoCoord& p, const GeoCoord& origin) {
    double phi = deg2rad(p.lat);
    double lam = deg2rad(p.lon);
    double phi0 = deg2rad(origin.lat);
    double lam0 = deg2rad(origin.lon);
    
    double sin_phi = std::sin(phi), cos_phi = std::cos(phi);
    double sin_phi0 = std::sin(phi0), cos_phi0 = std::cos(phi0);
    double d_lam = lam - lam0;
    
    // Radius of curvature in prime vertical
    double N = wgs84::a / std::sqrt(1.0 - wgs84::e2 * sin_phi * sin_phi);
    double N0 = wgs84::a / std::sqrt(1.0 - wgs84::e2 * sin_phi0 * sin_phi0);
    
    // ECEF deltas
    double dx = (N + p.h) * cos_phi * std::cos(lam) - (N0 + origin.h) * cos_phi0 * std::cos(lam0);
    double dy = (N + p.h) * cos_phi * std::sin(lam) - (N0 + origin.h) * cos_phi0 * std::sin(lam0);
    double dz = (N * (1.0 - wgs84::e2) + p.h) * sin_phi - (N0 * (1.0 - wgs84::e2) + origin.h) * sin_phi0;
    
    // Rotate to ENU
    double e = -std::sin(lam0) * dx + std::cos(lam0) * dy;
    double n = -sin_phi0 * std::cos(lam0) * dx - sin_phi0 * std::sin(lam0) * dy + cos_phi0 * dz;
    double u = cos_phi0 * std::cos(lam0) * dx + cos_phi0 * std::sin(lam0) * dy + sin_phi0 * dz;
    
    return {e, n, u};
}

double planar_shoelace_area(const std::vector<EnuCoord>& poly) {

    double sum = 0.0;

        size_t j = (i + 1) % n;
        sum += poly[i].e * poly[j].n - poly[j].e * poly[i].n;
    }
    return 0.5 * std::abs(sum);
}
```

```cpp
// Drone Photogrammetry: GSD computation, robust polygon area, and Ray‑DEM intersection
// Compile with: g++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -O2 -march=native -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer this_file.cpp && ./a.out

#include <cmath>
#include <vector>
#include <cassert>
#include <iostream>
#include <algorithm>
#include <limits>

constexpr double DEG2RAD = M_PI / 180.0;
constexpr double EPS = 1e-9;

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 1. Ground Sample Distance (GSD)
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
double computeGSD(double altitude_m,        // aircraft/drone altitude above ground (m)
                 double focalLength_m,     // focal length of camera (m)
                 double pixelSize_m,       // pixel pitch (m)
                 double latitude_deg) {    // geodetic latitude (deg)
    double latRad = latitude_deg * DEG2RAD;
    // Cosine of latitude corrects for convergence of meridians at high latitudes.
    double cosLat = std::cos(latRad);
    // Guard against division by zero at the poles.
    if (std::fabs(cosLat) < EPS) cosLat = EPS;
    return (pixelSize_m * altitude_m) / (focalLength_m * cosLat);
}

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 2. Robust polygon area (handles CW/CCW, mitigates catastrophic cancellation)
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
double polygonArea(const std::vector<std::pair<double,double>>& verts) {
    const size_t n = verts.size();
    assert(n >= 3);
    double sum = 0.0;
    double c = 0.0; // Kahan compensation
    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        const auto& [x0, y0] = verts[i];
        const auto& [x1, y1] = verts[(i + 1) % n];
        double term = x0 * y1 - x1 * y0;
        double y = term - c;
        double t = sum + y;
        c = (t - sum) - y;
        sum = t;
    }
    return std::fabs(sum) * 0.5;
}

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 3. Simple 3‑D vector utilities
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
struct Vec3 {
    double x, y, z;
    Vec3 operator+(const Vec3& o) const { return {x + o.x, y + o.y, z + o.z}; }
    Vec3 operator-(const Vec3& o) const { return {x - o.x, y - o.y, z - o.z}; }
    Vec3 operator*(double s) const { return {x * s, y * s, z * s}; }
    Vec3 normalized() const {
        double len = std::sqrt(x*x + y*y + z*z);
        assert(len > EPS);
        return {x/len, y/len, z/len};
    }
};

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 4. Bilinear height interpolation from a regular DEM grid
//    DEM is indexed as dem[row][col] where row increases northward, col eastward.
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
double sampleDEM(const std::vector<std::vector<double>>& dem,
                 double originX, double originY,   // world coordinates of DEM (0,0) corner (south‑west)
                 double cellSize,                 // spacing in metres
                 double x, double y) {            // query point in world coordinates
    double fx = (x - originX) / cellSize;
    double fy = (y - originY) / cellSize;
    int col0 = static_cast<int>(std::floor(fx));
    int row0 = static_cast<int>(std::floor(fy));
    int rows = static_cast<int>(dem.size());
    int cols = static_cast<int>(dem[0].size());

    if (col0 < 0 || row0 < 0 || col0 >= cols-1 || row0 >= rows-1)
        return -std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity(); // outside DEM → no terrain

    double dx = fx - col0;
    double dy = fy - row0;

    double h00 = dem[row0][col0];
    double h10 = dem[row0][col0+1];
    double h01 = dem[row0+1][col0];
    double h11 = dem[row0+1][col0+1];

    // Bilinear interpolation
    double h0 = h00 * (1 - dx) + h10 * dx;
    double h1 = h01 * (1 - dx) + h11 * dx;
    return h0 * (1 - dy) + h1 * dy;
}

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 5. Ray‑DEM intersection using bisection (robust for monotonic terrain)
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
bool intersectRayDEM(const Vec3& origin, const Vec3& dir,
                    const std::vector<std::vector<double>>& dem,
                    double demOriginX, double demOriginY,
                    double cellSize,
                    Vec3& outIntersection,
                    double maxDist = 1e5,
                    double tol = 1e-4) {
    // First, find an interval [t0,t1] where the ray goes from above terrain to below.
    double t0 = 0.0;
    double h0 = sampleDEM(dem, demOriginX, demOriginY, cellSize,
                          origin.x, origin.y);
    double f0 = origin.z - h0; // positive if ray start is above terrain
    if (f0 < 0) return false; // origin already below terrain

    double t1 = maxDist;
    double step = maxDist * 0.1;
    double t = step;
    while (t < maxDist) {
        Vec3 p = origin + dir * t;
        double h = sampleDEM(dem, demOriginX, demOriginY, cellSize, p.x, p.y);
        double f = p.z - h;
        if (f <= 0) { // crossed terrain
            t1 = t;
            break;
        }
        t += step;
    }
    if (t >= maxDist) return false; // never intersected within maxDist

    // Bisection refinement
    for (int iter = 0; iter < 60; ++iter) {
        double tm = 0.5 * (t0 + t1);
        Vec3 pm = origin + dir * tm;
        double hm = sampleDEM(dem, demOriginX, demOriginY, cellSize, pm.x, pm.y);
        double fm = pm.z - hm;
        if (std::fabs(fm) < tol) {
            outIntersection = pm;
            return true;
        }
        if (fm > 0) t0 = tm;
        else        t1 = tm;
    }
    outIntersection = origin + dir * 0.5 * (t0 + t1);
    return true;
}

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 6. Unit‑tests
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
int main() {
    // ---- GSD test (high latitude) ----
    double altitude = 500.0;                // metres
    double focalLen = 0.035;                // 35 mm → 0.035 m
    double pixelSize = 5e-6;                // 5 µm → 5e-6 m
    double lat = 78.22;                     // degrees north
    double gsd = computeGSD(altitude, focalLen, pixelSize, lat);
    // Expected value: (5e-6 * 500) / (0.035 * cos(78.22°)) ≈ 0.000714 m = 0.714 mm
    double expectedGSD = (pixelSize * altitude) / (focalLen * std::cos(lat * DEG2RAD));
    assert(std::fabs(gsd - expectedGSD) < 1e-12);

    // ---- Polygon area test (CW vs CCW) ----
    std::vector<std::pair<double,double>> squareCCW = {
        {0,0}, {10,0}, {10,10}, {0,10}
    };
    std::vector<std::pair<double,double>> squareCW = squareCCW;
    std::reverse(squareCW.begin(), squareCW.end());

    double areaCCW = polygonArea(squareCCW);
    double areaCW  = polygonArea(squareCW);
    assert(std::fabs(areaCCW - 100.0) < 1e-9);
    assert(std::fabs(areaCW  - 100.0) < 1e-9);
    assert(std::fabs(areaCCW - areaCW) < 1e-12);

    // ---- Ray‑DEM intersection tests ----
    // 1) Flat DEM (single cell at height 0)
    std::vector<std::vector<double>> demFlat = {{0.0}};
    Vec3 camPos{0.0, 0.0, 100.0};
    Vec3 dirDown = {0.0, 0.0, -1.0}.normalized();
    Vec3 hit;
    bool ok = intersectRayDEM(camPos, dirDown, demFlat,
                              -0.5, -0.5, 1.0, // origin at cell centre, cellSize 1 m
                              hit);
    assert(ok);
    assert(std::fabs(hit.x) < 1e-6 && std::fabs(hit.y) < 1e-6 && std::fabs(hit.z) < 1e-6);

    // 2) Sloped DEM (2×2, cellSize 10 m, heights 0 at (0,0) and 10 m at (10,10))
    std::vector<std::vector<double>> demSlope = {
        {0.0, 0.0},
        {0.0, 10.0}
    };
    // Camera above point (5,0) looking straight down.
    camPos = {5.0, 0.0, 100.0};
    ok = intersectRayDEM(camPos, dirDown, demSlope,
                         0.0, 0.0, 10.0,
                         hit);
    assert(ok);
    // Height at (5,0) = linear interpolation between (0,0)=0 and (10,0)=0 → 0.

    assert(std::fabs(hit.x - 5.0) < 1e-4);
    assert(std::fabs(hit.y - 0.0) < 1e-4);
    assert(std::fabs(hit.z - 0.0) < 1e-4);

    // 3) Sloped DEM with non‑vertical ray (45° towards +X)
    camPos = {0.0, 0.0, 100.0};
    Vec3 dir45 = {1.0, 0.0, -1.0}.normalized(); // 45° downwards towards +X
    ok = intersectRayDEM(camPos, dir45, demSlope,
                         0.0, 0.0, 10.0,

    // DEM height at x is (x/10)*10 = x (since height rises 1 m per metre in X)

    std::cout << "All tests passed.\n";
    return 0;
}
```

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Antimeridian‑safe great‑circle utilities.

* haversine_distance(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2) → meters
* great_circle_bbox(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2) → (min_lat, max_lat, min_lon, max_lon)

All angles are in decimal degrees, results in double‑precision (IEEE‑754) floats.
The bounding box uses the shortest great‑circle arc and correctly handles
cross‑antimeridian cases (min_lon > max_lon signals a wrap‑around).

The module contains a self‑test that validates the functions against an
analytical ground truth for a high‑latitude case (≈78.22° N) that stresses
numeric stability.
"""

import math
import sys

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constants
R_EARTH = 6371008.8          # mean Earth radius in metres (WGS‑84)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
def _deg2rad(d: float) -> float:
    return d * math.pi / 180.0

def _rad2deg(r: float) -> float:
    return r * 180.0 / math.pi

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
def haversine_distance(lat1: float, lon1: float,
                       lat2: float, lon2: float) -> float:
    """
    Return the great‑circle distance (metres) between two points using the
    haversine formula.  The implementation uses math.fsum to avoid
    catastrophic cancellation for very short distances.
    """
    φ1, φ2 = _deg2rad(lat1), _deg2rad(lat2)
    Δφ = φ2 - φ1
    Δλ = _deg2rad(lon2 - lon1)

    sin_dφ_2 = math.sin(Δφ * 0.5)
    sin_dλ_2 = math.sin(Δλ * 0.5)

    a = math.fsum([
        sin_dφ_2 * sin_dφ_2,
        math.cos(φ1) * math.cos(φ2) * sin_dλ_2 * sin_dλ_2
    ])
    # Clamp due to rounding errors (a may be slightly >1)
    a = min(1.0, max(0.0, a))
    return 2.0 * R_EARTH * math.asin(math.sqrt(a))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
def _unit_vector(lat: float, lon: float):
    """Return 3‑D Cartesian unit vector for given lat/lon (radians)."""
    φ = _deg2rad(lat)
    λ = _deg2rad(lon)
    cosφ = math.cos(φ)
    return (
        cosφ * math.cos(λ),   # x
        cosφ * math.sin(λ),   # y
        math.sin(φ)           # z
    )

def great_circle_bbox(lat1: float, lon1: float,
                      lat2: float, lon2: float):
    """
    Compute the latitude/longitude bounding box of the *shortest* great‑circle
    arc between the two points.  The returned longitudes are in the range
    [-180, 180]; if the arc crosses the antimeridian the box is expressed as
    (min_lon, max_lon) with min_lon > max_lon.
    """
    # ----- latitudes ----------------------------------------------------
    φ1, φ2 = _deg2rad(lat1), _deg2rad(lat2)

    # Unit vectors of the two points
    p1 = _unit_vector(lat1, lon1)
    p2 = _unit_vector(lat2, lon2)

    # Normal of the great‑circle plane (cross product)
    nx = p1[1] * p2[2] - p1[2] * p2[1]
    ny = p1[2] * p2[0] - p1[0] * p2[2]
```

/*
 * Production-Grade Spherical Excess Geodesic Polygon Area on WGS84
 * 
 * Algorithm: Authalic Sphere Projection + L'Huilier's Theorem (Triangulated Fan)
 *            with Hybrid Planar Fallback (Lambert Azimuthal Equal Area) for 
 *            sub-meter numerical stability.
 * 
 * Invariants:

 *  3. LAEA Planar projection exact for sphere, stable to machine epsilon for tiny polygons.
 *  4. IEEE-754 double precision enforced throughout.
 *  5. O(N^2) Self-intersection check; O(N) Collinearity/Duplicate check.

namespace wgs84 {
    constexpr double a       = 6378137.0;                 // Semi-major axis (m)
    constexpr double f       = 1.0 / 298.257223563;       // Flattening
    constexpr double e2      = 2*f - f*f;                 // Eccentricity squared
    constexpr double ep2     = e2 / (1.0 - e2);           // Second eccentricity squared
    
    // Authalic Radius R_A: Area(Sphere) = Area(Ellipsoid) = 4*pi*R_A^2
    // R_A = a * sqrt( (1 - e2/2 - ...) ) -> Closed form via q_p
    constexpr double q_p     = (1.0 - e2) * ( (1.0/(2.0*std::sqrt(e2))) * std::log((1.0+std::sqrt(e2))/(1.0-std::sqrt(e2))) - e2/(1.0-e2) );
    constexpr double R_A     = a * std::sqrt(0.5 * q_p);  // ~6371007.181 m

    // 1e-5 rad ~ 63m. 1e-6 rad ~ 6.3m. 
    // L'Huilier tan(E/4) loses precision when sides ~ 1e-6 due to tan(x)~x cancellation in sqrt prod.
    constexpr double PLANAR_THRESHOLD_RAD = 1e-5; 
    
    constexpr double PI      = 3.14159265358979323846;
    constexpr double DEG2RAD = PI / 180.0;
    constexpr double RAD2DEG = 180.0 / PI;
    
    // Machine epsilon guards
    constexpr double EPS     = 1e-15;  // Geometric zero (dot/cross mag)
    constexpr double EPS_ANG = 1e-14;  // Angular zero (radians)
}

struct Vec3 {
    double x, y, z;
    
    constexpr Vec3() : x(0), y(0), z(0) {}
    constexpr Vec3(double x_, double y_, double z_) : x(x_), y(y_), z(z_) {}
    
    Vec3& operator+=(const Vec3& o) { x+=o.x; y+=o.y; z+=o.z; return *this; }
    Vec3& operator-=(const Vec3& o) { x-=o.x; y-=o.y; z-=o.z; return *this; }
    Vec3& operator*=(double s)      { x*=s; y*=s; z*=s; return *this; }
    Vec3& operator/=(double s)      { x/=s; y/=s; z/=s; return *this; }
    
    friend Vec3 operator+(Vec3 a, const Vec3& b) { return a+=b; }
    friend Vec3 operator-(Vec3 a, const Vec3& b) { return a-=b; }
    friend Vec3 operator*(Vec3 a, double s)      { return a*=s; }
    friend Vec3 operator*(double s, Vec3 a)      { return a*=s; }
    friend Vec3 operator/(Vec3 a, double s)      { return a/=s; }
};

inline double dot(const Vec3& a, const Vec3& b) { return a.x*b.x + a.y*b.y + a.z*b.z; }
inline Vec3 cross(const Vec3& a, const Vec3& b) { 
    return Vec3(a.y*b.z - a.z*b.y, a.z*b.x - a.x*b.z, a.x*b.y - a.y*b.x); 
}
inline double norm2(const Vec3& a) { return dot(a, a); }
inline double norm(const Vec3& a)  { return std::sqrt(norm2(a)); }
inline Vec3 normalize(Vec3 a) { 
    double n = norm(a); 
    return (n > wgs84::EPS) ? a / n : Vec3(0,0,0); 
}

// Authalic Latitude Conversion: Geodetic (phi) -> Authalic (beta)
// q(phi) = (1-e^2) [ sin(phi)/(1-e^2 sin^2 phi) - 1/(2e) ln((1-e sin phi)/(1+e sin phi)) ]
// beta = asin( q(phi) / q(pi/2) )
inline double geodetic_to_authalic_lat(double phi_rad) {
    using namespace wgs84;
    double sin_phi = std::sin(phi_rad);
    double e = std::sqrt(e2);
    double sin_phi_e2 = e2 * sin_phi * sin_phi;
    
    // Stable computation of q(phi)
    // Term 1: sin / (1 - e^2 sin^2)
    double t1 = sin_phi / (1.0 - sin_phi_e2);
    
    // Term 2: atanh(e sin_phi) / e  <=> 1/(2e) ln((1+u)/(1-u)) where u = e sin_phi
    // Use std::atanh for |u|<1 stability
    double u = e * sin_phi;
    double t2 = (std::abs(u) < 1.0 - 1e-15) ? std::atanh(u) / e : 0.0; // Limit at poles handled by t1 dominance
    
    double q_phi = (1.0 - e2) * (t1 - t2);
    
    // q_p (q at pi/2) precomputed as constant q_p
    double ratio = q_phi / q_p;
    // Clamp for safety at poles due to rounding
    if (ratio > 1.0) ratio = 1.0;
    if (ratio < -1.0) ratio = -1.0;
    
    return std::asin(ratio);
}

// Convert Geodetic (Lat, Lon Deg) -> Unit Vector on Authalic Sphere
inline Vec3 geodetic_to_authalic_vec(double lat_deg, double lon_deg) {
    double lat_rad = lat_deg * wgs84::DEG2RAD;
    double lon_rad = lon_deg * wgs84::DEG2RAD;
    
    double beta = geodetic_to_authalic_lat(lat_rad);
    double cos_beta = std::cos(beta);
    
    return Vec3(
        cos_beta * std::cos(lon_rad),
        cos_beta * std::sin(lon_rad),
        std::sin(beta)
    );
}

// Central angle (side length) between two unit vectors. Stable via atan2(|cross|, dot).
inline double spherical_side(const Vec3& a, const Vec3& b) {
    Vec3 cr = cross(a, b);
    double cr_n = norm(cr);
    double dt = dot(a, b);
    // Clamp dt for acos safety, but atan2 handles it naturally
    return std::atan2(cr_n, dt); 
}

// Signed Area (Excess) of Spherical Triangle via L'Huilier's Theorem
// Inputs: sides a, b, c (radians). Assumes a >= b >= c for stability.
inline double lhuilier_excess(double a, double b, double c) {
    using namespace wgs84;
    // Semi-perimeter
    double s = 0.5 * (a + b + c);
    
    // Arguments for tan
    double ts  = std::tan(0.5 * s);
    double tsa = std::tan(0.5 * (s - a));
    double tsb = std::tan(0.5 * (s - b));
    double tsc = std::tan(0.5 * (s - c));
    
    // Product under sqrt. For very small triangles, args -> 0, tan(x) ~ x.
    // Guard against negative due to rounding (s-a < 0)
    double prod = ts * tsa * tsb * tsc;
    if (prod <= 0.0) return 0.0; // Degenerate or numerical noise
    
    double tan_E4 = std::sqrt(prod);
    // E = 4 * atan(tan(E/4))
    return 4.0 * std::atan(tan_E4);
}

// Planar Fallback: Lambert Azimuthal Equal Area (LAEA) Projection at Center 'c'
// Maps sphere to plane preserving area. Excess = Planar Area of Projected Triangle.
inline double planar_excess_laea(const Vec3& c, const Vec3& a, const Vec3& b) {
    // Basis at center c: East (x), North (y)
    // East = Normalize( Z x c ) where Z = (0,0,1)
    // North = c x East
    Vec3 Z(0,0,1);
    Vec3 east = cross(Z, c);
    double east_n = norm(east);
    
    // Handle center at pole (east_n == 0)
    Vec3 north, e_norm;
    if (east_n < wgs84::EPS) {
        // At pole, arbitrary basis: East = (1,0,0), North = (0,1,0) aligned with Lon=0
        e_norm = Vec3(1,0,0);
        north  = Vec3(0,1,0);
        if (c.z < 0) north = Vec3(0,-1,0); // South pole orientation
    } else {
        e_norm = east / east_n;
        north  = cross(c, e_norm); // Already unit length
    }
    
    // LAEA Projection: k = sqrt(2 / (1 + dot(v, c)))
    // Coords: x = k * dot(v, East), y = k * dot(v, North)
    // For tiny triangles near c, k ~ 1. 
    // We compute signed area of triangle (c, a, b) in this plane.
    // Since c projects to (0,0), area = 0.5 * | a_x*b_y - a_y*b_x |
    
    auto project = [&](const Vec3& v) -> std::pair<double, double> {
        double dot_vc = dot(v, c);
        // Clamp dot_vc to [-1, 1] for safety
        if (dot_vc > 1.0) dot_vc = 1.0;
        if (dot_vc < -1.0) dot_vc = -1.0;
        double k = std::sqrt(2.0 / (1.0 + dot_vc));
        double x = k * dot(v, e_norm);
        double y = k * dot(v, north);
        return {x, y};
    };
    
    auto [ax, ay] = project(a);
    auto [bx, by] = project(b);
    
    // Signed area (c is origin)
    return 0.5 * (ax * by - ay * bx);
}

void validate_polygon(const std::vector<Vec3>& verts) {
    size_t n = verts.size();

        size_t ip1 = (i + 1) % n;

    }
    
    // 3. Self-Intersection Check (O(N^2) Great Circle Arc Intersection)
    // Arcs (Vi, Vi+1) and (Vj, Vj+1) intersect properly if:
    // sign(triple(Vi, Vi+1, Vj)) != sign(triple(Vi, Vi+1, Vj+1)) AND
    // sign(triple(Vj, Vj+1, Vi)) != sign(triple(Vj, Vj+1, Vi+1))
    // Ignore adjacent edges (share vertex) and same edge.
    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        size_t ip1 = (i + 1) % n;
        Vec3 n1 = cross(verts[i], verts[ip1]); // Normal to plane 1
        double n1_norm = norm(n1);
        if (n1_norm < wgs84::EPS) continue; // Degenerate edge caught above
        
        for (size_t j = i + 1; j < n; ++j) {
            size_t jp1 = (j + 1) % n;
            
            // Skip adjacent edges (share vertex)
            if (i == j || ip1 == j || i == jp1 || ip1 == jp1) continue;

            if (i == 0 && jp1 == 0) continue;

            Vec3 n2 = cross(verts[j], verts[jp1]);
            double n2_norm = norm(n2);
            if (n2_norm < wgs84::EPS) continue;

            // Triple products
            double t1a = dot(n1, verts[j]);
            double t1b = dot(n1, verts[jp1]);
            double t2a = dot(n2, verts[i]);
            double t2b = dot(n2, verts[ip1]);

            if (cross1 && cross2) {
                throw ValidationError("Self-intersection detected between non-adjacent edges.");
            }
        }
    }
}

namespace s2_geodesy {

struct WGS84 {
    static constexpr long double a  = 6378137.0L;           // Semi-major axis (m)
    static constexpr long double f  = 1.0L / 298.257223563L; // Flattening
    static constexpr long double e2 = 2.0L * f - f * f;     // Eccentricity squared
    
    // Authalic Radius (R_A): Radius of sphere with same surface area as ellipsoid
    // R_A = a * sqrt( (1 - e^2/2 - ...) ) -> Exact integral form:
    // q(phi) = (1-e^2) * ( sin(phi)/(1-e^2 sin^2(phi)) - 1/(2e) ln((1-e sin)/(1+e sin)) )
    // R_A = a * sqrt( q(pi/2) / 2 )
    static constexpr long double authalic_radius() noexcept {
        const long double e = sqrtl(e2);
        const long double e2_ = e2;
        // q_p = q(pi/2)
        // Limit phi->pi/2: sin=1. Term1 = 1/(1-e^2). Term2 = 1/(2e) ln((1+e)/(1-e))
        const long double term1 = 1.0L / (1.0L - e2_);
        const long double term2 = (1.0L / (2.0L * e)) * logl((1.0L + e) / (1.0L - e));
        const long double q_p = (1.0L - e2_) * (term1 - term2);
        return a * sqrtl(q_p / 2.0L);
    }

    // Authalic Latitude (beta) from Geodetic Latitude (phi)
    // sin(beta) = q(phi) / q_p
    static long double geodetic_to_authalic_lat(long double phi_rad) noexcept {
        const long double e = sqrtl(e2);
        const long double sin_phi = sinl(phi_rad);
        const long double e_sin = e * sin_phi;
        const long double denom = 1.0L - e2 * sin_phi * sin_phi;
        
        long double q_phi;
        if (fabsl(denom) < 1e-18L) { // Pole
            q_phi = (1.0L - e2) * (1.0L / (1.0L - e2) - (1.0L/(2.0L*e))*logl((1.0L+e)/(1.0L-e)));
        } else {
            const long double term1 = sin_phi / denom;
            const long double term2 = (1.0L / (2.0L * e)) * logl((1.0L + e_sin) / (1.0L - e_sin));
            q_phi = (1.0L - e2) * (term1 - term2);
        }
        
        const long double e_ = e;
        const long double term1_p = 1.0L / (1.0L - e2);
        const long double term2_p = (1.0L / (2.0L * e_)) * logl((1.0L + e_) / (1.0L - e_));
        const long double q_p = (1.0L - e2) * (term1_p - term2_p);
        
        const long double sin_beta = q_phi / q_p;
        // Clamp for safety
        return asinl(std::max(-1.0L, std::min(1.0L, sin_beta)));
    }
};

    long double s = sinl(theta * 0.5L);
    return s * s;
}

// Inverse Haversine: theta = 2 * asin(sqrt(h)). Stable for small h.
inline long double ahav(long double h) noexcept {
    if (h <= 0) return 0.0L;
    if (h >= 1) return M_PIl;
    return 2.0L * asinl(sqrtl(h));
}

// Central Angle (Side Length) between two unit vectors. 
// Uses haversine formula on vectors: hav(theta) = |u-v|^2 / 4
inline long double central_angle(const Vec3& u, const Vec3& v) noexcept {
    long double dx = u.x - v.x;
    long double dy = u.y - v.y;
    long double dz = u.z - v.z;
    long double h = (dx*dx + dy*dy + dz*dz) * 0.25L;
    return ahav(h);
}

// Signed Area (Excess) of Spherical Triangle via L'Huilier's Theorem
// tan(E/4) = sqrt( tan(s/2) tan((s-a)/2) tan((s-b)/2) tan((s-c)/2) )
// Returns Excess E in radians. Sign determined by winding order (handed separately).
long double lhuilier_excess(long double a, long double b, long double c) noexcept {
    // Semi-perimeter
    const long double s = (a + b + c) * 0.5L;
    
    // Arguments for tan half-angles
    // For numerical stability on tiny triangles (a,b,c ~ 1e-6), 
    // tan(x) ~ x. Product ~ (s/2)*((s-a)/2)*... 
    // We compute in log-space if args are tiny? No, long double (1e-4932 range) handles 1e-6^4 = 1e-24 easily.
    // However, catastrophic cancellation in (s-a) if a~b~c.
    // s-a = (b+c-a)/2. This is stable.
    
    const long double s_half = s * 0.5L;
    const long double sa_half = (s - a) * 0.5L;
    const long double sb_half = (s - b) * 0.5L;
    const long double sc_half = (s - c) * 0.5L;
    
    // Guard against negative args due to rounding (degenerate triangles)
    if (sa_half <= 0 || sb_half <= 0 || sc_half <= 0) return 0.0L;
    
    // Compute product of tans
    // tan(x) for small x is accurate in long double.
    long double prod = tanl(s_half) * tanl(sa_half) * tanl(sb_half) * tanl(sc_half);
    
    if (prod <= 0) return 0.0L;
    
    long double E_over_4 = atanl(sqrtl(prod));
    return 4.0L * E_over_4;
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------
// Polygon Area Accumulator (Kahan-Babuska-Neumaier Summation)
// ------------------------------------------------------------
class AreaAccumulator {
    long double sum_ = 0.0L;
    long double c_ = 0.0L; // Compensation
public:
    void add(long double value) noexcept {
        long double t = sum_ + value;
        if (fabsl(sum_) >= fabsl(value)) 
            c_ += (sum_ - t) + value;
        else 
            c_ += (value - t) + sum_;
        sum_ = t;
    }
    long double value() const noexcept { return sum_ + c_; }
    operator double() const noexcept { return static_cast<double>(value()); }
};

// ------------------------------------------------------------
// Main API: Geodesic Polygon Area on WGS84 (Authalic Sphere)
// ------------------------------------------------------------
/**
 * Computes the area of a geodesic polygon on the WGS84 ellipsoid
 * by mapping vertices to the Authalic Sphere and applying 
 * Spherical Excess (L'Huilier) via fan triangulation.
 * 
 * @param vertices Vector of (longitude_deg, latitude_deg) pairs. 
 *                 Polygon must be closed (first == last) or open (auto-closed).
 *                 Winding order: CCW = Positive Area (Standard GIS).
 * @return Area in square meters (double precision).
 */
double geodesic_polygon_area_wgs84(const std::vector<std::pair<double, double>>& vertices_ll) {
    const size_t n_raw = vertices_ll.size();
    if (n_raw < 3) return 0.0;
    
    // Check if closed
    bool closed = (vertices_ll.front().first == vertices_ll.back().first && 
                   vertices_ll.front().second == vertices_ll.back().second);
    size_t n = closed ? n_raw - 1 : n_raw;
    if (n < 3) return 0.0;

    // 1. Convert Geodetic (Lon, Lat) -> Authalic Sphere Unit Vectors
    std::vector<Vec3> verts;
    verts.reserve(n);
    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        long double lon = vertices_ll[i].first  * (M_PIl / 180.0L);
        long double lat = vertices_ll[i].second * (M_PIl / 180.0L);
        long double beta = WGS84::geodetic_to_authalic_lat(lat);
        verts.push_back(Vec3::from_spherical(lon, beta));
    }

    // 2. Fan Triangulation from Vertex 0
    // Area = Sum( Excess(v0, vi, vi+1) ) * R_A^2
    // Sign of excess determined by scalar triple product (v0, vi, vi+1) dot v0_normal?
    // Actually, sign of excess is determined by winding order of vertices on sphere.
    // We compute signed excess using the orientation of the triangle normal.
    
    AreaAccumulator acc;
    const Vec3& v0 = verts[0];
    
    for (size_t i = 1; i + 1 < n; ++i) {
        const Vec3& v1 = verts[i];
        const Vec3& v2 = verts[i+1];
        
        // Side lengths (central angles)
        long double a = central_angle(v1, v2); // opposite v0
        long double b = central_angle(v2, v0); // opposite v1
        long double c = central_angle(v0, v1); // opposite v2
        
        // Spherical Excess (Magnitude)
        long double E = lhuilier_excess(a, b, c);
        
        // Sign: Determined by the orientation of the triangle (v0, v1, v2)
        // Normal n = (v1 - v0) x (v2 - v0) projected? 
        // On unit sphere, the signed area is proportional to the solid angle.
        // Sign = sign( v0 . (v1 x v2) )  [Scalar Triple Product]
        // This gives positive for CCW winding when viewed from outside sphere (standard).
        long double stp = v0.dot(v1.cross(v2));
        if (stp < 0) E = -E;
        
        acc.add(E);
    }
    
    long double area_m2 = acc.value() * (R_AUT * R_AUT);
    return static_cast<double>(area_m2);
}

// High-precision Local Tangent Plane (ENU) projection for Ground Truth
// Origin: Svalbard Reference Point (78.22 N, 16.0 E)
struct LocalENU {
    double lat0_rad, lon0_rad;
    double sin_lat0, cos_lat0;
    double R_mer, R_prime; // Meridional and Transverse radii of curvature at origin
    
    LocalENU(double lat0_deg, double lon0_deg) {
        lat0_rad = lat0_deg * M_PI / 180.0;
        lon0_rad = lon0_deg * M_PI / 180.0;
        sin_lat0 = sin(lat0_rad);
        cos_lat0 = cos(lat0_rad);
        
        const double a = 6378137.0;
        const double f = 1.0 / 298.257223563;
        const double e2 = 2*f - f*f;
        const double sin2 = sin_lat0 * sin_lat0;
        const double W = sqrt(1.0 - e2 * sin2);
        R_mer = a * (1.0 - e2) / (W * W * W); // Meridional radius
        R_prime = a / W;                       // Transverse (Prime Vertical) radius
    }
    
    // Geodetic -> ENU (meters)
    std::pair<double, double> forward(double lat_deg, double lon_deg) const {
        double lat = lat_deg * M_PI / 180.0;
        double lon = lon_deg * M_PI / 180.0;
        double dLat = lat - lat0_rad;
        double dLon = lon - lon0_rad;
        
        // Rigorous local projection (Tangent Plane)
        // North = R_mer * dLat
        // East  = R_prime * cos(lat0) * dLon
        double N = R_mer * dLat;
        double E = R_prime * cos_lat0 * dLon;
        return {E, N}; // (Easting, Northing)
    }
    
    // ENU -> Geodetic (Inverse)
    std::pair<double, double> inverse(double E, double N) const {
        double dLat = N / R_mer;
        double dLon = E / (R_prime * cos_lat0);
        double lat = lat0_rad + dLat;
        double lon = lon0_rad + dLon;
        return {lat * 180.0 / M_PI, lon * 180.0 / M_PI};
    }
};

// Planar Shoelace Formula (Ground Truth for Local Planar Polygon)
double planar_shoelace_area(const std::vector<std::pair<double, double>>& pts_xy) {
    size_t n = pts_xy.size();
    if (n < 3) return 0.0;
    double A = 0.0;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        size_t j = (i + 1) % n;
        A += pts_xy[i].first * pts_xy[j].second;
        A -= pts_xy[j].first * pts_xy[i].second;
    }
    return fabs(A) * 0.5;
}
